ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Annual Wellness Visit, Subsequent — Jim Bridger

text.paragraph: Mr. Bridger, 70, comes for his subsequent annual wellness visit four weeks after his fifteen-week review; his last wellness visit was a year ago at his previous clinic. Both cataract operations are behind him and with his new glasses he recognizes faces across the yard, reads the large numbers on his phone and has started driving into town again by day. His wrist has healed. His back aches less since physical therapy and he does his exercises most mornings. He walks the orchard every day. He asked about the shingles vaccine after a neighbor had shingles. [S]

tr.td: Lens implants in both eyes after cataract surgery; chronic low back pain; multinodular goiter; knee osteoarthritis; one fall with a wrist sprain this spring
Diclofenac 1% gel on the knees as needed; no other medicines or supplements

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-08-18; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 76.9 kg, BMI 23.0; blood pressure 130/76; pulse 64 and regular
Both eyes quiet; pupils round and reactive
Ear canals clear; whispered voice missed at arm's length on the left
Firm, nodular goiter, unchanged, moving with swallowing; no nodes; trachea midline
Regular rhythm; no murmur; no carotid bruit; foot pulses present
Weathered, sun-damaged skin on the face and hands with several rough scaly patches on the backs of the hands; old scar on the right lower back
Right wrist full range without tenderness; knee crepitus; Timed Up and Go 10 seconds

Gradual, painless blurring of vision in both eyes over about two years, worse in the right, with glare from sunlight and oncoming headlights, faded colors, and trouble recognizing faces across a room; Snellen acuity 20/200 right and 20/100 left with his old glasses, no better with a pinhole; no flashes, floaters, pain or redness; cause under evaluation with an ophthalmology consultation
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to his documented failing eyesight; superseded when the consultation found bilateral cataract.

Bilateral age-related nuclear cataract, dense and brunescent in the right eye and moderate in the left, with cortical spokes; the cause of his reduced vision, glare and color loss; no glaucoma, macular degeneration or diabetic retinopathy; treated with sequential cataract surgery
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the consultation, linked to his documented loss of sight; not a retrospective diagnosis of his real blindness, whose cause is not recorded.

Chronic low back pain for many years, aching across the lower back and worst on the side of an old arrow-wound scar over the right lower back, stiff in the morning and after long rides in his truck; no leg pain, numbness, weakness, bladder or bowel change, fever or weight loss; no red flags
S — Synthetic chronic back pain anchored to his documented arrow wound; which side of the back the arrowhead lay in is not recorded, and the right side is a synthetic choice.
Nontoxic multinodular goiter, present for decades: a firm, nodular, non-tender thyroid enlargement with no pressure symptoms (no trouble swallowing or breathing, no voice change); euthyroid
S — Synthetic modern classification of his documented goiter; the type of his real goiter is not recorded.
Primary osteoarthritis of both knees, aching on stairs and after walking the orchard, with morning stiffness under half an hour, crepitus and bony enlargement
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to his documented rheumatism; the old term does not name a modern diagnosis.
One fall in the past year, missing the bottom step of the porch at dusk, without injury; poor vision in low light and contrast; at risk of further falls
S — Synthetic fall linked to the reduced vision.
Sprain of the right wrist from a fall on the porch steps three weeks after the first cataract operation, when the two eyes saw differently; X-ray without fracture; healed
S — Synthetic acute injury at the sick visit; not a historical claim.
Lens implants in both eyes after sequential phacoemulsification cataract surgery, right then left six weeks apart; best-corrected vision about 20/20 in each eye with new glasses
S — Synthetic status after the modern cataract surgery.

Subsequent annual wellness visit completed. Health risk assessment reviewed aloud and the prevention plan updated. Lipid panel: total cholesterol 188, HDL 56, LDL 112 and triglycerides 98 mg/dL; with blood pressure 130/76, no diabetes and no tobacco, his 10-year cardiovascular risk is in the intermediate range for his age, but he has none of the risk factors (dyslipidemia, diabetes, hypertension or smoking) that the USPSTF uses to recommend a statin. After a shared decision he chose not to start a statin and to revisit it next year. Hearing loss on the whispered voice test and sun-damaged skin with probable actinic keratoses were found. [S]

Follow-up: Six-month review in six weeks. Hepatitis results by phone. Second zoster dose in two to six months; influenza and COVID-19 vaccines in the autumn. Audiology and dermatology appointments made. Next wellness visit in one year. Next scheduled visit 2026-09-29: six-month review: back pain on a home program, knees, falls, the goiter and the plan ahead. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with his consent. He named a health care agent and a health care proxy form was completed, read aloud to him before he signed; the agent is recorded in the chart and is not named here. He said what matters most is staying on his own land, seeing the country around him, and not being kept alive on machines if he could not recover to know the people around him. The plan will be revisited yearly or after any serious illness. [S]
